main_statement.latex: \begin{theorem}[Critical local smoothing] For every $\eps>0$ there exists $C_\eps<\infty$ such that $\norm{Uf}_{L^3(\R^3\times[1,2])} \le C_\eps\norm{J^\eps f}_{L^3(\R^3)}$ $(f\in\mathcal S(\R^3))$.\end{theorem}
main_statement.paraphrase: The half-wave evolution e^{it sqrt(-Delta)} maps W^{eps,3}(R^3) to L^3(R^3 x [1,2]) for every eps>0: at the critical exponent p=3 = 2n/(n-1) (n=3), time averaging recovers the full fixed-time loss 1/3 up to an arbitrary eps. Interpolation with L^2 and an L^infty kernel bound gives Corollary 9.6: ||Uf||_{L^p(R^3x[1,2])} <= C ||J^alpha f||_p for 2<p<infty, alpha>max{0,1-3/p}, i.e. Sogge's Euclidean local smoothing conjecture in 3+1 dimensions (strict, eps-loss form). The lossless endpoint eps=0 is explicitly not addressed (00:45-46).
headline_corollaries: Cor 9.7 (09:651-687): maximal half-wave sup_{0<t<1}|Uf| bounded W^{s,p}->L^p for p>=3, s>1-2/p; a.e. convergence (via BHS survey eq 3.24).
Thm 10.1 (10:21-96): maximal Bochner-Riesz B_*^delta bounded on L^p(R^3), 3<=p<infty, delta>1-3/p; a.e. summation (via BHS Prop 3.3).
Cor 10.2 (10:98-133): Bochner-Riesz conjecture in R^3, full strict range delta>max{3|1/p-1/2|-1/2,0}, 1<=p<=infty (via BHS Prop 3.2, interpolation, duality).
10:145-163: spherical extension ||Eg||_{L^r(R^3)} <= C ||g||_{L^r(S^2)}, r>3 (Tao 1999) - the full diagonal restriction conjecture for S^2.
10:165-193: Kakeya maximal estimate ||K_h F||_{L^3(S^2)} <= C_eps h^-eps ||F||_3 (Wolff 1999 Prop 4.1).
main_statement.relation_to_known_results: Before: GWZ 2020 settled 2+1 (critical p=4) via the sharp cone square function / wave-envelope estimate; Bourgain-Demeter decoupling gives 3+1 for p>=4; GLMX 2023 gave alpha>1/9 at p=3; Gan-He-Li-Wu (arXiv 2502.05973v2, Jan 2026) give the sharp gain for p>=10/3 in 3+1 (and sharp results on manifolds for odd n), hence alpha>1/12 at p=3 by interpolation; Rozendaal-Schippa (arXiv 2608.01440, Aug 2026) alpha>2/9 at p=3 for rough coefficients. On manifolds the full gain fails for p<10/3 (Minicozzi-Sogge), so any p=3 proof must use Euclidean structure; here it enters via GWZ's Euclidean cone wave-envelope theorem, the exact round-cone/null-hyperquadric geometry and Bateman's conformal covariance. The paper uses GWZ's 2+1 theorem as a lower-dimensional INPUT (on parabolic-cylinder sections), not as a special case. Web search (Oct 2026) found no other claimed resolution of 3+1 local smoothing.

proof_architecture.claim: Reduce Thm 1.1 to a single frequency annulus H^{-1}: ||W_H g||_3 <= C H^{-delta}||g||_3 (Prop 9.1), then Littlewood-Paley summation.

Null coordinates turn the annular half-wave into a free round-cone wave (rays (A,|A|^2)); bounded-amplitude pieces of L^3 data give round experiments with energy e~||g||_2^2 and regularity kappa = H^-gamma B^2 on all round and hyperquadric tests; synthesis bounds int|v|^3 by H^{-1/2} sum m^{3/2}.
Thm 8.1: round exponent Gamma <= 100 eta. By contradiction: take extremal (p,d), Gamma=d+(1-p)/2, benchmarks E_a, kappa_a.

Thin terminal shapes (f with positive exponent) are reduced to cylinder experiments by flattening a null hyperquadric with a conformal (Bateman) chart; the transformed wave becomes a classical or hybrid (quantum-normal) cylinder experiment.

Thm 2.4: cylinder exponents <= eta/2. Extremal reduction: saturation of splits, matched gates with compatible shears (M), Planck floor, minimal shear costs c, c1, Lipschitz width profiles, shape constraints, affine profiles (F).

Zero-cost cases excluded by lower-dimensional inputs: hybrid via GWZ wave envelope (kinetic + scalar channel), classical via conditional Ren-Wang incidence bootstrap (D'(a)>=1+3d vs D(1)<=1+3d-2Gamma).
Positive-cost cases: canonical names C(a,v) recording time, shear frame, base and residual normal phase; entropy excess E(a,v) >= 0 with E=0 at boundary points recovered from labels.
Conditional replicas, walks, projection rule and radial dichotomy (Ren-Wang) give rate inequalities; these yield local actions (d_a - k d_v)E >= 2Gamma.
Path argument: follow characteristics backward from boundary points; E would become negative. Case analysis over (c, J, q, d) closes Thm 2.4.

Round labels at uncertainty scale: round phase names, excess E(a,v)=D-4v-(p+d)a>=0, E(a,u(a))=0; outgoing entropy o_T >= 4d+min(1-d,m/2) via four transverse pins and Ramsey; classical case integrates directly, wave case by the two-direction descent lemma.
Corollaries: full range by interpolation; maximal half-wave; Bochner-Riesz (maximal and nonmaximal), sphere restriction, Kakeya maximal via cited implications.

correctness_audit.verdict: No gap located, but verification was far from complete: Secs 0-2, 9-10 and the closing proofs of Thms 2.4 and 8.1 were read; Secs 3-8 (about 9,350 lines) only at statement level. Arithmetic spot checks pass. This is an extraordinary claim (it would also settle Bochner-Riesz, sphere restriction and Kakeya maximal in R^3) supported only by an unrefereed, unformalised, extremely compressed text. Treat as unverified.
checked: Exponent algebra: Gamma=d+(1-p)/2 from (cyl:functional); p<3 from Gamma>0, d<=1; p+d=1+3d-2Gamma (04:15). Correct.

Thm 8.1 wave closing (08:1452-1467): with E=D-4v-(p+d)a, t=1-a: E_t=1+3d-2Gamma-o_T; E_v<=m+o_T-d-3. If m<=2-2d then o_T>=4d+m/2>=m+5d-1 gives E_t+E_v/2<=-2Gamma; if m>=2-2d then o_T>=1+3d gives E_t<=-2Gamma. Verified by hand.
Two-direction descent lemma (08:1384-1431): argument along lines parallel to the zero-trace boundary plus a vertical escape is correct for Lipschitz E with m monotone in t.
Classical round case: D'(a,0)>=1+3d vs D(1,0)<=p+d=1+3d-2Gamma. Consistent.
Synthesis lemma (09:379-440): |v|<~H^{-3/2} m^{1/2} on an H-cube, cell volume H^4, gives H^{-1/2} m^{3/2}. Correct.

Input regularity (09:211-375): predecessor volume r^4 f via Jacobian r^4/(1+|A|^2) and degree-2 sublevel bound with gradient lower bound from the discriminant identity; weight floor r^4 f^{1-eta}>=H^2. Plausible and checked at the level of the displayed algebra.
Amplitude decomposition (09:484-515): B_nu ||g_nu||_2^2 <= 2||g_nu||_3^3, log many levels. Standard restricted-type argument; correct.
Ren-Wang formulation F(a,b)=a+min{1,b,(a+b)/2} = min(a+1,a+b,(3a+b)/2) matches the Furstenberg bound min(s+t,(3s+t)/2,s+1) (arXiv 2308.08819 abstract).
Hilbert-valued GWZ via complex Gaussian randomisation (03:57-78): E|<v,G>|^2|<w,G>|^2 = ||v||^2||w||^2+|<v,w>|^2. Correct.
One-time bound (02:323-350) and peeling (02:375-405): routine, correct as written.
Corollary chain: LS => BR (BHS Prop 3.2/3.3) => restriction (Tao) => Kakeya maximal (Wolff). These implications are established; the exponents quoted match (n=3: threshold 1-3/p for p>=3).
consistency_checks_passed: Euclidean structure is used where it must be: the manifold counterexamples (Minicozzi-Sogge) need p>=10/3; the proof uses the exact round cone, conformal covariance and the Euclidean GWZ theorem.
No claim of the lossless endpoint; Bochner-Riesz maximal range p>=3 only, consistent with what local smoothing implies.
Prior record at p=3 (alpha>1/12 from Gan-He-Li-Wu v2; alpha>1/9 GLMX) is correctly reported (GHLW abstract checked: sharp on manifolds for odd n, i.e. p>=10/3 for n=3).
residual_concerns: Extraordinary scope: simultaneous resolution of four major R^3 conjectures by a single unrefereed model-produced paper; prior probability of a fatal gap is substantial.

Heavy reliance on 'exponent closure' and ordered limits (Sec 1): extremal configurations exist only in a closure of finite experiments; many steps assert that constants 'depend only on eta, not on the mesh' (02:746-747) or that errors are o(h) after earlier limits. The paper itself warns of failure modes (Remark fw-extra-coordinate; the B_m diagonal example 01:299-305), indicating fragility.

Case analysis completeness in the proof of Thm 2.4 (06:1083-1276): many regimes (c<1, c=1, 1<c<=3, c>3; J ranges; strict q<1 with d<C1/(1+2C1); strong vs weak alternatives; hybrid vs classical). Missing or overlapping-condition errors would be fatal and are hard to see without full verification.

Hybrid (quantum) model: entropy arguments are run on artificial classical rays extended backward from quantum samples (04:36-41), justified only through the Planck floor (Pl); positivity of phase-space laws for masked quantum evolution is explicitly not claimed. Risky step.

Many lemma statements carry hypotheses phrased as 'with probability tending to one' or 'typical', combined later with pigeonholing and Ramsey; uniformity across the finite query lists is asserted but not displayed.
Ren-Wang's paper (arXiv 2308.08819v3) has no journal reference listed on arXiv as of Oct 2026; the input is accepted by the community but unrefereed formally.
No reasoning trace, no Lean, no independent check; companion papers 074/077/078 share machinery, so an error in a common tool could propagate across all four.

Many key objects are tagged equations rather than environments: (M),(A),(B),(F),(Pl),(Sp),(canon),(surplus),(excess),(round-out),(mem),(SC),(kin),(RW),(inc).

Symbol overloading: D = normal position / endpoint depth / profile D(a) / D(a,v) / D_0; J = Bessel potential / profile slope / interval function J(a,v,w); E = energy / excess; H = Planck parameter / entropy / mode coordinate; p = Lebesgue exponent / mass exponent.
Definitions inside proofs and paragraphs (crossing energy 03:756; nested name C(a) 03:1340; marks (xi) 04:624; phase name (grid) 08:537; transverse event 08:1207).
Two parallel developments (cylinder Secs 2-6, round Secs 7-8) with analogous but distinct names, excesses and descent arguments; joined items P86/P87/P88 are numbered out of sequence.
Many statements are deliberately qualitative-exponent statements ('s^{o(1)}', 'typical', 'in the closure'), so equivalence checks against neighbours need human judgement.
Family shares vocabulary with same-release papers 074, 077, 078 (excess, upper exponent, hybrid, cylinder, canonical profile); naive cross-family matching would conflate them.
